subject: Trial SKU mapping & checkout CTA — AWS listing readiness
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS listing help — trial SKU and CTA question

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're getting the final asset pack together for the AWS listing and hit two items I wanted your input on before we push to the partner portal:

1) Trial SKU mapping — our product team wants to expose a "30-day trial" as a SKU on the marketplace so customers can spin up a trial instance. AWS requires entitlements configuration. Can Redwood confirm whether a trial SKU counts as a separate entitlement or if it should be handled via PrivateOffer/Trial link? Attached is our current SKU table.

2) Checkout CTA wording — we want the hero CTA to be simple but accurate for procurement teams. Options we've drafted: 
   - "Start free 30-day trial"
   - "Request trial (Private Offer)"
   - "Start self-serve trial"

Which phrasing better aligns with Redwood's recommended flow and reduces procurement confusion? If there are copy/legal constraints for marketplace pages, please flag them.

I've uploaded the listing draft here: https://drive.google.com/redwood/listing-draft and attached the SKU table (sku_mapping_v1.csv). Our timeline: goal to submit by next Tuesday (Aug 3).

Appreciate any quick guidance and happy to hop on a 20-min sync if that's easier.

Best,
Sasha Patel
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp
Phone: +1 415 555 0134

--
Attachment: sku_mapping_v1.csv (CSV, 78KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing help — trial SKU and CTA question

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear note and upload. Quick responses inline and next steps below.

1) Trial SKU mapping: recommend we model the trial as a distinct SKU that maps to a time-limited entitlement in the marketplace metadata, not as a Private Offer. That preserves self-serve discovery and keeps procurement flows simple. Redwood's infra can route the trial SKU to a short-lived entitlement (30 days) and automatically revoke at expiration. I've attached a suggested mapping (sku_mapping_v1.csv updated) showing entitlement_id, duration_days, and fallback model.

2) Checkout CTA wording: my recommendation is "Start free 30-day trial" for the hero CTA and then surface a secondary "Contact sales / Request Private Offer" link in the pricing/entitlement section. The hero CTA reduces friction; the secondary link covers procurement-driven customers. Avoid "Request trial" alone because it sets expectation of a manual sales step.

Next steps:
- Kimberly: can you review the hero CTA phrasing and confirm there's no compliance/legal restriction for the wording?
- Aditya: can you validate the entitlement revocation workflow and confirm we can support the SKU mapping in the partner portal by Aug 3?
- Sasha: if you can confirm the final SKU names, we'll fold them into the listing draft and push to the partner portal submission queue.

If helpful, I'm free for a 20-min call today at 3:00pm PT or tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood_listing_v2.docx (DOCX, 210KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing help — trial SKU and CTA question

Thanks Logan — quick copy + ops notes from my side. Quoting Logan below for context.

> 2) Checkout CTA wording: my recommendation is "Start free 30-day trial" for the hero CTA and then surface a secondary "Contact sales / Request Private Offer" link in the pricing/entitlement section.

Short suggestions for the product page:
- Hero headline: "Try Redwood Inference — free for 30 days" (keeps "try" verb, which performs well in UX tests).
- Hero CTA: "Start free 30-day trial" (primary, prominent).
- Secondary CTA (text link under primary): "Request a private offer" (targets procurement).
- Pricing footnote: include a short line: "Trial entitlements are time-limited and automatically expire; contact sales for enterprise licensing."

Operational checks:
- Ensure the SKU names are stable (no spaces, lowercase) to avoid portal munging. Recommend sku keys like: acme_trial_30d, acme_prod_monthly.
- Add analytics tag: marketplace_cta=trial_hero for A/B measurement. We'll need the cta_test_matrix.xlsx filled with expected volumes for each variant. I've started a matrix and attached it.

Marissa — can you review tone and the pricing footnote? I think the legal-friendly phrasing above is fine but want marketing's sign-off.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Marketplace GTM | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

--
Attachment: cta_test_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)

From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS listing help — trial SKU and CTA question

Thanks everyone — this is helpful. Quoting Kimberly.

> Hero CTA: "Start free 30-day trial" (primary, prominent).
> Secondary CTA (text link under primary): "Request a private offer" (targets procurement).

We're comfortable with that structure. A couple of follow-ups:
- Timeline: we need the final SKU names and the updated listing doc by EOD Monday (Aug 2) so our procurement and legal teams can do a last pass before submission to AWS on Aug 3. Can you confirm you can meet that?
- Procurement note: AWS partner portal may surface the trial as a separate SKU to buyers. We might need to add a short seller note on the product page about billing ("No automatic billing after trial; customers choose a subscription at end of trial"). Can Redwood confirm that message is acceptable?

If it's easier to finalize on a short call, Tom and I can join. Proposed 30-min sync tomorrow 9:30am PT.

Thanks again — Sasha
Sasha Patel
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp
